uncertainties.note: The source uses the SAME katakana word for the drive (book 1) and for its developer's surname (2044), and the line's point is that the two match. Locked glossary spellings differ: 'Baldora Drive' vs 'Jill Bardona'. Locked spellings were used, which hides the link in English; the glossary should be unified (both provisional).
'B Plan' for the New Federation development programme named with the letter B; 'Project B' is the more natural English but contains the missing j glyph. See proposals.
Speaker formerly belonged to the New Federation (candidates: Holland, Jamil); not tagged, line works for either.
Berkt rendered 'him' per glossary gender (male). Speaker refers to Hayato familiarly; speaker not identified. 'he's the one with the details' - 'he' = Hayato.
Source says the priest 'that (people are) after' is aboard 'that'; whose target the priest is (allies' objective or enemy's) is left open with 'everyone's after'. Vehicle not named in source.

First half is an unfinished 'with this...'; second half is the bare organisation name plus an emphatic/derisive particle, shouted. Rendered as an attack shout; could also be read as exasperation at the Railway.
1984 praises someone's performance without naming them; 1985 'we' supplied for natural English (relief that the train made it).
Per-character taunt exchanges with the Rushrod pilot; player-side speakers unidentified. 1996 'old geezer' renders a rude 'old man' term.
2002-2003 are the Rushrod pilot facing an unfamiliar (other-world) machine; 2004/2005 replies by unidentified pilots.

Long window lines compressed to fit 110 visible characters; 2028 (exactly 110) 'Your company would help' compresses 'it would help if you acted together with us'. 2041 clause order changed (development history before 'trump card') to keep the book span around New Federation in place.
'the colonies' = the colony side (Gundam X Space Revolutionary Army context); organisation name not supplied because source does not give it.
Two colour spans in source order: ship name first, personal name second; name in Western order per glossary (Ruri Hoshino).
